question: True or false: a toughened glass panel can shatter by itself, years after fitting, with nothing touching it?
answer: True. The best-known culprit is a speck of nickel sulphide trapped when the glass was made. Toughening freezes it in a high-temperature crystal form; over months or years it reverts and swells by a few per cent, enough to release the stress stored in the pane. Baking panes at about 290 °C weeds most out.
move: A flaw can wait years for the conditions that set it off.
trap: Glass only breaks when something hits it or bends it.
source: EN 14179, heat soaked toughened safety glass
reference: EN 14179-1:2005, Glass in building — Heat soaked thermally toughened soda lime silicate safety glass — Part 1: Definition and description
